$comment: Misconception catalogue. 'implicates' lists skills whose weakness this misconception is evidence of; the detour planner intersects it with the prerequisite closure of the failed skill. Awaiting named human review with the templates that use these tags.

misconceptions.description: Gives the total distance travelled when asked for displacement.

flashcard.front: Is displacement the total distance travelled?
flashcard.back: No. Displacement is the change in position (final − initial), with a direction; path length is the total distance covered.

misconceptions.description: Gives the change in position when asked for the distance travelled.

flashcard.front: A walk out and back: is the path length the same as the displacement?
flashcard.back: No. Path length adds every stretch travelled; displacement only compares the start and end.

misconceptions.description: Drops the sign (direction) of a displacement.

flashcard.front: Can a displacement be negative?
flashcard.back: Yes. Its sign gives its direction along the axis: negative means towards −x.

misconceptions.description: Uses only the last stretch of a journey as the displacement.

flashcard.front: Displacement for a two-stage journey?
flashcard.back: Final position minus initial position, not just the last stage.

misconceptions.description: Divides metres by minutes and reports the result as m/s.

flashcard.front: Distance in m, time in min: is d ÷ t in m/s?
flashcard.back: No. Convert minutes to seconds first (× 60).

misconceptions.description: Averages two speeds arithmetically when equal distances are covered at each.

flashcard.front: Half the distance at v₁, half at v₂: average speed?
flashcard.back: 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂), not (v₁ + v₂) ÷ 2: more time is spent at the slower speed.

misconceptions.description: Uses total distance ÷ time when average velocity is asked.

flashcard.front: Average velocity or average speed: which uses displacement?
flashcard.back: Average velocity = displacement ÷ time; average speed = path length ÷ time.

misconceptions.description: Averages the velocities of the stages instead of dividing displacement by total time.

flashcard.front: Is average velocity the mean of the stage velocities?
flashcard.back: Only if the stages take equal times. In general, total displacement ÷ total time.

misconceptions.description: Reads a negative x–t slope as slowing down.

flashcard.front: A straight x–t line sloping down: what is happening?
flashcard.back: Constant velocity in the −x direction. Slope is velocity; a straight line means it doesn't change.

misconceptions.description: Reads a position–time graph as a picture of the path.

flashcard.front: Is an x–t graph a picture of the route?
flashcard.back: No. It shows position against time; its slope is the velocity.

misconceptions.description: Divides one position by one time instead of using the change in position.

flashcard.front: Velocity from an x–t line?
flashcard.back: Slope = Δx ÷ Δt between two points, not x ÷ t at one point.

misconceptions.description: Uses run over rise for a slope.

flashcard.front: Slope of a straight-line graph?
flashcard.back: Rise over run: change in the vertical quantity ÷ change in the horizontal one.

misconceptions.description: Uses the average velocity from t = 0 instead of the tangent's slope.

flashcard.front: Instantaneous velocity on a curved x–t graph?
flashcard.back: The slope of the tangent at that instant, not x ÷ t.

misconceptions.description: Reads the position at an instant as the velocity.

flashcard.front: On an x–t graph, is the height of the curve the velocity?
flashcard.back: No. The height is the position; the slope is the velocity.

misconceptions.description: Uses v ÷ t for acceleration, ignoring the initial velocity.

flashcard.front: Acceleration from u to v in time t?
flashcard.back: a = (v − u) ÷ t: the change in velocity per unit time.

misconceptions.description: Adds the velocities instead of subtracting them.

flashcard.front: Is acceleration (u + v) ÷ t?
flashcard.back: No: (v − u) ÷ t.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies the final velocity by the whole time.

flashcard.front: Displacement from a v–t graph?
flashcard.back: The area under it: a sloping part makes a triangle or trapezium, not a rectangle of height v.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the accelerating part of the v–t area.

flashcard.front: v–t graph: acceleration phase then constant speed. Distance?
flashcard.back: Triangle (acceleration) + rectangle (constant speed).

misconceptions.description: Leaves the initial velocity out of v = u + at.

flashcard.front: v = u + at: what does u add?
flashcard.back: The velocity the body already had; a t is only the change.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the distance covered during the reaction time.

flashcard.front: Stopping distance with a reaction time?
flashcard.back: Thinking distance u·t_r plus braking distance u² ÷ 2a.

misconceptions.description: Drops the ½ in v² = u² + 2as (or s = ut + ½at²).

flashcard.front: Braking distance from u at deceleration a?
flashcard.back: u² ÷ (2a): the 2 comes from v² = u² + 2as.

misconceptions.description: Gives the distance fallen when the speed is asked.

flashcard.front: Speed after falling for t seconds from rest?
flashcard.back: v = g t (the distance is ½ g t²).

misconceptions.description: Gives the time to the top when the height is asked.

flashcard.front: Maximum height of a ball thrown up at u?
flashcard.back: u² ÷ (2g); the time to the top is u ÷ g.

misconceptions.description: Uses the time to return to the launch height when the ball lands lower.

flashcard.front: Ball thrown up from a cliff top: time to the ground below?
flashcard.back: Solve h + ut − ½gt² = 0 with the cliff height; 2u/g only brings it back to the top.

misconceptions.description: Treats a thrown ball as simply dropped.

flashcard.front: Thrown up from a cliff vs dropped: same time to land?
flashcard.back: No. The upward throw adds time going up and coming back.

misconceptions.description: Adds the velocities of bodies moving the same way.

flashcard.front: Velocity of A relative to B, both moving the same way?
flashcard.back: v_A − v_B.

misconceptions.description: Subtracts speeds of bodies approaching each other.

flashcard.front: Two cars approaching head-on: closing speed?
flashcard.back: The sum of their speeds.

misconceptions.description: Uses only one train's length for an overtaking time.

flashcard.front: Time for one train to pass another completely?
flashcard.back: (L₁ + L₂) ÷ relative speed.

misconceptions.description: Adds the speeds of trains moving the same way.

flashcard.front: Relative speed of trains moving the same way?
flashcard.back: The difference of their speeds.

misconceptions.description: Uses only u·t for the distance, ignoring the speed gained.

flashcard.front: Is the distance u × t when the body speeds up?
flashcard.back: No. Add the triangle ½(v − u)t for the speed gained.

misconceptions.description: Uses only the triangle above the starting speed.

flashcard.front: Area under a sloping v–t line from u to v?
flashcard.back: A rectangle u·t plus a triangle ½(v − u)t.

misconceptions.description: Uses the slope of a v–t graph when the area is asked.

flashcard.front: What does the area under a v–t graph give?
flashcard.back: The displacement. The slope gives the acceleration.

misconceptions.description: Drops the ½ in the braking-distance formula.

flashcard.front: Braking distance from u at deceleration a?

misconceptions.description: Uses u instead of u² in the braking-distance formula.

flashcard.front: Double the speed: braking distance?
flashcard.back: Four times as large: s = u² ÷ (2a).

misconceptions.description: Gives the stopping time u ÷ a when the distance is asked.

flashcard.front: Stopping time or stopping distance: u ÷ a or u² ÷ (2a)?
flashcard.back: u ÷ a is the time; u² ÷ (2a) is the distance.
